description:
Capability for the main window. Every permission below is scoped to the narrowest path/URL it needs — see the note on each block for why it exists and why its scope is what it is. (JSON has no comment syntax and Tauri capability files only parse as JSON or TOML, not JSON5 — TOML's own capability shape isn't documented with confidence, so the rationale lives here instead of splitting across two config formats.)

- dialog:allow-open / dialog:allow-save — the native file/folder picker. Phase 1 already calls `open()` (backup folder, .apkg import) and `save()` (Markdown export) from `@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`; today it works only because dialog ACL enforcement hasn't shipped yet. `dialog:default` also grants `allow-message`/`allow-ask` (native alert/confirm popups) which nothing in this app calls, so only the two commands actually used are listed.
- fs:allow-exists / fs:allow-mkdir / fs:allow-write-file — the three plugin-fs calls `storeMediaFile` (src/features/editor/blocks/media/media-storage.ts) makes to persist EDT-024..027 media (image/video/audio/file blocks): check the media/ subfolder exists, create it if not, write the deduplicated-by-hash file. No allow-read-file / allow-remove / allow-rename because nothing in the app calls them — the WebView reads media back through the asset: protocol (see app.security.assetProtocol below), not through plugin-fs.
- fs:scope — restricts all three fs commands above to `$APPDATA/media` and its contents only, never `fs:default`'s app-wide scope. This covers the common case where the user has not overridden the data directory (Phase 1's `get_data_dir`/`save_data_dir` default to null, and `mediaDirPath()` falls back to `appDataDir()` exactly then). KNOWN GAP: a user who points `save_data_dir` at a custom folder gets media writes outside this static scope and `storeMediaFile` will fail — fixing that needs a Rust-side runtime scope extension (`app.fs_scope().allow_directory(..)`) called from wherever `save_data_dir` is handled, which lives in src-tauri/src/config or src-tauri/src/ipc — outside this task's file ownership. Left as a follow-up, not silently widened to `$APPDATA/**` or beyond to paper over it.
- app.security.assetProtocol (tauri.conf.json) — enabled with the same `$APPDATA/media/**` scope, so `convertFileSrc()` can resolve a written file into a URL the WebView is actually allowed to load; see that file's own comment.
- http:default — outbound fetch for EDT-028 bookmark metadata (src/features/editor/blocks/bookmark/metadata.ts), via tauri-plugin-http (runs on the Rust side, not subject to the page's CORS policy the way in-WebView `fetch` is). Allows any http/https URL, because the user pastes whatever URL they want bookmarked — but denies localhost and every RFC1918/link-local/loopback range (10.*, 172.16-31.*, 192.168.*, 169.254.* incl. the cloud metadata IP, 127.*, 0.0.0.0, and their IPv6 equivalents) on both schemes, so a direct paste can't be used to probe the user's own machine or local network. `file:` needs no explicit deny: the http plugin only ever dials http/https, so a `file:` URL is already rejected by the plugin itself, not by this scope. KNOWN LIMIT, not fixable from this file: this scope is checked once against the URL fetch() is *called with* — tauri-plugin-http never re-checks it against a `Location:` redirect hop, so a public URL that 302s to a private IP sails through this ACL untouched. That's why `isPrivateOrLoopbackHost` (src/features/editor/blocks/bookmark/bookmark-card.ts) exists and is the real gate — applied in metadata.ts to both the initial target and `response.url` after every redirect. Do not treat this deny list as sufficient on its own; it only narrows what a first hop can dial.
